ruleName: Playing the ball as it lies
title: When must you NOT play the ball as it lies?
question: Which situation means you are NOT allowed to play the ball as it lies?

choices.text: The ball is out of bounds
The ball is on the wrong green
The ball is in a no play zone, like a protected young tree area

explanation: You must not play a ball as it lies if it is out of bounds, on the wrong green, or in a designated no play zone. In these cases, you must take relief or apply the relevant rule.

juniorVersion.title: When should you NOT hit the ball where it stopped?
juniorVersion.question: In which of these places are you NOT allowed to hit your ball from where it is?

choices.text: The ball is outside the golf course (out of bounds)
The ball is sitting on the wrong green
The ball is in a spot with signs saying 'no playing', like around young trees

juniorVersion.explanation: You are not allowed to hit your ball where it stopped if it is outside the course, on another green, or in a place where you cannot play (like a protected tree area). If this happens, you must follow the rules to move your ball.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means your ball has gone outside the area of the golf course where you are allowed to play.
This is a green for a different hole. You cannot play your ball from here.
A place on the course where you must not hit the ball, like around young trees.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Explain to juniors that sometimes the rules make them move their ball to care for the course and to keep everyone safe.
likelyMisconceptions: Some juniors may think they can hit from anywhere the ball stops.
They might not know what a no play zone or wrong green means.
